title: Fix the Split-and-Sum
statement: The program below is meant to do the following: read an integer n, then a line with n integers (possibly negative). Split the list into a first half (the first n // 2 elements) and a second half (the rest). Print two numbers on one line: the sum of the non-negative values (>= 0) in the first half, and the sum of the non-negative values in the second half. The code below has 3 bugs. Fix them so it passes all test cases.
starter_code:
n = int(input())
nums = list(map(int, input().split()))
half = n // 2
first = nums[0:half - 1]
second = nums[half:n]
total = 0
for x in first:
    if x > 0:
        total += x
first_total = total
for x in second:
    if x >= 0:
        total += x
second_total = total
print(first_total, second_total)
hints: Check the slice bound used to build 'first' - does it include every element of the first half?
The spec says non-negative (>= 0), but one of the two loops uses a strict > 0 check
'total' is never reset before the second loop, so second_total ends up including first_total too
